newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel firm on tight supply, barges bounce up.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel firm on tight supply, barges bounce up.

text.p: High sulphur cracked barges bounded higher on Monday reaching a peak of over $4 against Friday's levels.
Traders said a barge was done at $112.50 in the afternoon although subsequent deals were seen at $111.50. The barge market was active even though physical bunker demand was assessed poor.
"It's just people playing around with the market," said one broker. Supplies, however, were seen to be reasonably tight.
High sulphur cracked cargoes were also firmer, but not to the same degree.
Prices continued to take comfort from the rally last week which saw $109 fob NWE done, caused by the bullish Iraqi news and tightness to cover the last Portuguese tender.

The low sulphur cargo market was also seen a touch firmer as physical material slowly closed the gap on swaps numbers. Sept paper traded at $111.50 fob NWE and there was little reason for sellers to accept the $106 fob NWE seen on Friday.
"There's a steep curve against the balance of September -- bidders want fixed prices, sellers are looking for floating," said one dealer.
